clue.text: Evelyn had boy evolving into a star, perhaps

indicators.note: evolving means changing form, so the letters of these three words develop into a new order

explanation.surface: Evelyn's baby boy is growing up to be a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evolving' rearranges EVELYN, HAD and BOY; 'star' wants to mean a celebrity but is the astronomical sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is one example of a celestial object, along with planets and moons.

clue.text: She may give the order to belt up

definitions.text: She may give the order to belt up

parts.words: She may give the order to belt up
parts.note: belt up sounds like rude slang for be quiet, but here it is the instruction to passengers on a plane to fasten seatbelts, given by cabin crew

explanation.surface: A woman telling someone rudely to shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: An air stewardess announces that passengers must fasten their seatbelts before take-off.

clue.text: Oil stirred into premier mayonnaise

indicators.note: into tells us the stirred letters go inside the word for premier

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, premier; written AI

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so the letters of oil are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cook mixing oil into top-quality mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: Premier is read as A1, first-class, written with the letter I standing for the digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic-flavoured Provençal kind of the egg-and-oil sauce.

clue.text: Highlight English pies and mash getting cooked

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stressing the British fare of pies and mash being prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting cooked' rearranges E, PIES and MASH; pie and mash is a traditional London working-class meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight a point is to stress or give it prominence.

clue.text: Bush — one of a comedy pair

explanation.definitionFit: A bay tree is an evergreen shrub; Stan of that surname partnered Oliver Hardy in classic film comedy.

clue.text: As the sun shines on a coastal resort?

parts.note: when the sun shines things are bright
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sunshine falling on a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one picture of sunshine; the resort is a seaside town on England's south coast, in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known English seaside town in Sussex, famous for its pier.

clue.text: Drab? No good getting involved with home improvements

indicators.note: getting involved with places the abbreviation for no good inside the home improvements term

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself, home improvements done by the owner

explanation.surface: A dreary house where do-it-yourself projects never come out well.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull, shabby and lacking brightness, as of a gloomy room.

clue.text: I could be lauded as inventive?

definitions.text: I could be lauded as inventive?

indicators.note: inventive suggests creative reworking, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to be praised for creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inventive' rearranges LAUDED AS; the whole clue is also the definition, since the mythical figure was the great inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mythical craftsman built the Labyrinth and wings for Icarus, so he would be praised for ingenuity.

clue.text: A place for out-of-this-world experiments

parts.note: out-of-this-world suggests marvellous, but literally means in orbit, beyond Earth

explanation.surface: Somewhere for amazing scientific research.
explanation.definitionFit: The first US space station orbited Earth in the 1970s, a laboratory in orbit.

clue.text: Bank's backing this ship

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a pool is a common fund or bank of money; with the 's it becomes pools

explanation.surface: A bank financially supporting a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' wants to mean financial support, but reverses POOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Something to lift a marriage? It's the standard

parts.note: a marriage is a union
a jack is a device for lifting a car

explanation.surface: Asking what could cheer up a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK national flag; 'standard' here means a flag, not a norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Doolittle, say, to gamble on hot girl

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl of Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady
to bet is to gamble
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone betting on an attractive young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Doolittle is a surname, so the first name is wanted; 'on' places H after BET.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Country bumpkin's heart turned to daughter's song

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is changed into another letter

parts.note: a yokel is a country bumpkin
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A rustic's affections switching to his daughter's singing.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of YOKEL is K; 'heart turned to' swaps it for D.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbling Alpine style of singing that flips between registers.

clue.text: Interference that won't go away

explanation.definitionFit: Crackling on a radio is called by this name; something fixed and unmoving is also described so.

clue.text: Dear gran, dreadfully dressed

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Grandmother wearing awful clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' rearranges DEAR GRAN; 'dressed' means set out, as a window display is dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out in order, as hair or a shop window display is set out.

clue.text: Iron perhaps, and the place to use it

explanation.surface: An iron and where it is used on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is one kind of stick used in the game; the society and its course share the name.

clue.text: Fish struggles in mud

explanation.surface: Fish floundering in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatfish of the plaice family; also flails about clumsily, as when stuck in mire.

clue.text: A sort of bowler not getting enough ammo

parts.note: under means insufficient, as in underfed
an arm is a weapon, loosely ammunition

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler short of firepower.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowling below shoulder height; 'bowler' wants to mean a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a delivery with the hand kept below the shoulder, a style of bowling.

clue.text: Bilko, eg, in mad rage among cast

indicators.note: among puts the scrambled letters in the middle of the word for cast

parts.note: to cast is to throw, so cast means sent

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A TV character furious with the rest of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bilko is the scheming US Army rank-holder of 1950s TV comedy, played by Phil Silvers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Bilko held this non-commissioned army rank in The Phil Silvers Show.

clue.text: Head of Science relaxes with time coming up to worry

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word
in a down entry the letter for time rises to the top of the word

parts.note: rests means relaxes

explanation.surface: A scientist relaxing yet anxious as time runs short.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'coming up' means moving towards the top, so the time letter shifts to the front of the word for relaxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety or pressure; to fret.

clue.text: Relative from America in the money?

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for America inside the word for money

parts.note: coin means money

explanation.surface: Wondering if a relative from America is rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of one's aunt or uncle, a family member.

clue.text: Incessant number beginning to niggle bar

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: to bar is to stop

explanation.surface: Constant small irritations at the start of a pub visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuing without pause or a break.

clue.text: Dog set about porridge, say

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog starting on a bowl of porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, filling food; oatmeal cereal is a typical example.

clue.text: Replace sausage I left in return

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter goes out
in return means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a wiener is a frankfurter sausage

explanation.surface: Swapping a sausage that someone returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns WIENER into RENEIW; 'left' removes I.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to restore or put a fresh one in place.

clue.text: Renegue on bet with Dai's family?

explanation.surface: A Welshman dodging a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh is to avoid paying a debt; Dai is a typical Welsh name, so his family is of Wales.

clue.text: This could prolong former troubles

parts.note: ex means former
tension means strain or trouble

explanation.surface: Old difficulties dragging on.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition that lengthens something, like extra time added to a deadline.

clue.text: One spreading game's profile

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: spreading means scattering, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the 's is no letter here

explanation.surface: Someone popularising a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Public image or reputation, as in a high public persona.

clue.text: A group of Caribbean rappers?

parts.note: rappers suggests hip-hop artists but means people who strike drums made of oil barrels

explanation.surface: A band of West Indian hip-hop artists.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trinidadian ensemble playing pans made from oil drums.

clue.text: Elicit precise fine

explanation.surface: Drawing out an accurate penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand or extract; also accurate and correct.

clue.text: I clear stacks of debris

parts.note: stacks suggests piles of rubbish, but means chimney stacks cleared of soot

explanation.surface: A cleaner tidying up heaps of mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who brushes soot out of flues.
